A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive rewriting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original circuit-discovery experiments involving data resampling, hyperparameter variation, and injected noise, with additional results in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original measurements comparing exact causal-mediation edge scores with EAP estimates on GPT-2 small and IOI.

M1.justification: The four EAP-family estimators remain unchanged. Exact CMA is added as an experimental reference, without establishing a modification to the circuit-discovery algorithms. Bayesian discovery and stability objectives remain future proposals.

E1.justification: Both versions use IOI, Subject-Verb Agreement, and Greater-Than, retaining the resampling, paraphrasing, and embedding-noise scenarios. The new exact-CMA analysis uses the existing IOI coverage rather than introducing another task or population.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds exact CMA, described as exact edge ablation, as a reference comparator for EAP in one diagnostic experiment. The existing circuit comparisons retain EAP, EAP-IG-inputs, EAP-IG-activations, and Clean-corrupted. HAP and RelP are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 Section 5.1 introduces a distinct evaluation design: computing exact causal effects for every edge and input in GPT-2/IOI and comparing edge-score distributions with EAP. Existing circuit metrics and model configurations remain. The noise description also changes from fixed-direction perturbations to Gaussian sampling, although the PDFs do not establish that the retained noise experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new edge-score analysis investigates whether variability already exists in exact causal effects and how approximate scores differ. This substantially extends v1's analyses of final circuit stability. The earlier resampling, hyperparameter, and noise analyses remain, including their appendix displays.

E5.justification: v3 Section 3.4 specifies 100 bootstrap datasets, whereas v1 mentions seed-iterated runs without that count. This is newly disclosed repetition information, not evidence of increased runs. Existing circuit means, variances, coefficients of variation, and standard-deviation bands retain their reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 Figure 2 and Section 5.1 add central findings: exact edge scores often have CV around 0.5, while EAP scores often exceed 1 despite generally smaller means and standard deviations. Retained circuit results match, including Table 1's bootstrap error 0.440 and Jaccard 0.561. Appendix Tables 6 and 7 exchange numbers without changing their results.

T1.justification: v3 substantially replaces the generic discovery formalization with an explicit natural-indirect-effect definition in Equation 1, a population importance target defined as an expectation over input-counterfactual pairs, and circuit selection from estimated scores. These specify the statistical estimand and its relationship to discovery; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims that EAP-IG circuits are unstable under perturbations. v3's abstract and introduction claim a broader explanation: instability originates in exact CMA, is amplified by approximation, and propagates through aggregation into circuit structure. The recommendation for statistically rigorous interpretability remains.

C2.justification: v3 interprets noise amplitude as changing the counterfactual question and attributes circuit instability to intrinsic variability, approximation, and aggregation. New Section 6.3 qualifies generalization beyond GPT-2/IOI, the EAP family, and three discrete linguistic tasks, and acknowledges that unweighted edge overlap may obscure a stable functional core.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies the EAP-IG library and default hyperparameters, but removes v1's greedy-selection details: absolute scores, starting at 30 edges, increasing up to 2000, and stopping upon connectivity. It also removes the public-codebase statement; this does not establish that code access was withdrawn.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands from an EAP-IG stability case study to a claimed first systematic decomposition across the CMA-to-circuit pipeline. New discussions connect the work to statistical stability, identifiability, bootstrapped edge selection, HAP, and RelP. These include Bousquet and Elisseeff, Preston, and Nikankin; several earlier motivation references, including Adebayo and Heap, disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, formal setup, retained-results discussion, and recommendations are extensively rewritten and reorganized. v3 introduces numbered discussion subsections, explicit limitations, an impact statement, and appendix navigation. The title and EAP terminology also change.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text and references from one column to two, adds the edge-score histogram and distribution figure, and substantially resizes and relocates existing displays. Retained plots are renumbered, and appendix tables are reordered; their plotted data and numerical contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit causal estimand, exact-CMA comparison in Figure 2, and substantive limitations make the statistical argument better supported and easier to assess. The gain is constrained: the new experiment covers only GPT-2/IOI and compares relative variability without quantitatively decomposing approximation error, while explicit circuit-selection details disappear. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement rather than a substantial overall gain.
